title: Customer service AI: The guide for growing businesses
summary: Unlock customer service AI for your business and enhance efficiency, boost customer satisfaction, and drive growth.
body_markdown:
##


Key takeaways


- Customer service AI uses natural language processing, machine learning, and large language models to answer customers, automate routine tasks, and resolve issues quickly.
- The main types of customer service AI are chatbots, AI agents, AI copilots, voice AI, intelligent routing, and sentiment analysis. Each handles a different part of your support workflow.
- The biggest risks, like inaccurate answers and unpredictable costs, have practical fixes so you can implement AI into your business.
- Start with one problem, like missed calls, and expand once you know your approach works.


It’s the question on every small business owner’s mind: when to hire more support reps.


This is a tricky question. You have to balance providing your customers with a great experience with your budget. Couple that with the necessary ramp-up time, fluctuations in support volume, and finding the right person to represent your brand… Well, it can be *daunting* .


But if you wait too long, you risk burying your existing reps in emails, tickets, and other support requests. They’ll be overwhelmed, and the customer experience will suffer.


AI-powered customer service can solve many of these challenges. By integrating AI into your customer service workflows, you can handle higher volumes, free up your reps to handle more complex issues, and still provide an outstanding customer experience.


We’ll cover what customer service AI is, the main types of AI tools available to you, 11 ways to integrate[AI into your small business](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-ai/) , and how to roll out AI effectively.


##


**What is customer service AI?**


Customer service AI is technology that can understand customer requests, answer questions, automate routine tasks, and help human reps resolve issues faster. It can work on its own, like an AI agent that answers calls, or alongside your team, like a writing tool that drafts replies.


Here’s how it works:


- Natural language processing, or NLP, lets AI understand what customers say or type, even when they don’t use the exact words in your help articles.
- Machine learning helps the AI spot patterns in past conversations and improve over time.
- Large language models, or LLMs, power generative AI, which writes new, contextually relevant responses instead of picking from a list of pre-set answers.


Newer tools also use agentic AI. For context, generative AI tools create content, such as a reply or a call summary. Agentic AI goes a step further and takes action on its own. For example, agentic AI tools can take messages, book appointments, and send follow-up texts to help ensure customer satisfaction.


AI in customer service is quickly becoming the norm.[Gartner predicts](https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/customer-service-ai) that by 2028, at least 70% of customers will use a[conversational AI](https://www.quo.com/blog/conversational-ai/) interface to help start their customer service journey.


##


**Types of customer service AI**


Type What is does Best for


Chatbots Answer common questions in chat using natural language Businesses with a lot of repetitive website or app questions


AI agents Have conversations and take action on their own, like taking messages or booking appointments Teams that miss calls or messages during busy times and after hours


AI copilots Suggest replies, summarize conversations, and surface answers for reps Teams that want to help reps work faster


Voice AI and IVR Understand spoken requests, then answer or route calls Businesses that get a lot of phone calls


Intelligent routing Send each conversation to the best person or team Teams with several departments or specialists


Sentiment analysis and conversation analytics Spot customer emotions, trends, and process gaps Managers who oversee service quality


### **Chatbots**


Chatbots talk with customers through your website, app, or messaging channels. AI-powered chatbots use NLP to understand questions written in plain language and access answers from your knowledge base.


You may also hear the terms “virtual agents” and “virtual assistants.” These advanced customer service chatbots handle structured tasks, like checking order statuses, within paths you design ahead of time. When a request falls outside those paths, they hand the conversation to a real person.


### **AI agents**


AI agents handle conversations from start to finish and take action on their own.


These customer service AI tools run on LLMs, so they can understand the context of a request and choose the next step without a script. Many people use the term “agentic AI” to describe this category.


Adoption is climbing fast. According to[Salesforce’s State of Service research](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/ai-service-agents-improve-customer-satisfaction/) , 66% of customer service organizations now use agentic AI, up from 39% in 2025. For example,[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s AI agent, helps customer service teams by answering calls 24/7, taking messages, and booking appointments.


### **AI copilots**


AI copilots, sometimes referred to as agent assist tools, work alongside human reps. They follow the conversations your team has and suggest replies, summarize past interactions, and pull answers from your knowledge base. Your reps stay in control and decide what to send.


In Quo, our AI[call summaries](https://www.quo.com/features/call-summary) and[transcripts](https://www.quo.com/features/call-transcriptions) include automatically generated action items from phone calls to help reps follow up faster.


### **IVR and Voice AI**


Interactive voice response, or IVR, is the phone menu that asks callers to “Press one for billing, press two for sales,” etc. Voice AI uses voice recognition and NLP, so callers can say what they need in their own words.


Some voice assistants answer the question on the spot, while others route the call to the right person. Sona can do both. Equally as important, it works inside your[call flows](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/call-flow-software) and alongside your[phone menus](https://www.quo.com/product/menu-routing) .


### **Intelligent routing**


[Intelligent routing](https://quo.com/blog/intelligent-call-routing) uses AI to send each call, chat, or support ticket to the best person or team based on who the customer is and what they need. Machine learning and predictive analytics help routing improve over time, keeping your staff from getting buried when ticket volume spikes.


For instance, Quo offers AI call routing features. When enabled, Sona transfers each caller to the teammate who’s best equipped to help, a strategy known as skill-based routing.


### **Sentiment analysis and conversation analytics**


[Sentiment analysis](https://www.quo.com/blog/sentiment-analysis-tools/) uses AI to detect whether customers sound happy, confused, or frustrated. Conversation analytics evaluate interactions to spot trends, like a spike in billing questions.


Together, these tools help protect your customer satisfaction scores, or CSAT, and fix problems before they spread. In Quo, you can use AI call tags to sort calls into categories you choose based on customer sentiment, billing requests, or other categories you want to easily track.


##


**Benefits of customer service AI for small businesses**


AI can solve many logistical challenges for small business customer service teams, such as staffing and providing prompt, accurate replies to customers. But the benefits extend beyond your customers and your team.


### **Make your company available 24/7**


According to[Zendesk’s CX Trends 2026 report](https://www.zendesk.com/in/blog/zendesk-insights/trends/leading-in-the-ai-era-with-contextual-intelligence/) , 74% of consumers expect customer service to be available 24/7. AI agents and chatbots cover nights, weekends, and busy periods, so customers get help even when your team is offline. It also makes it easier to win new business because potential customers can get the information they need from your AI, instead of calling a competitor.


### **Build a more efficient and productive team**


With AI, customer service teams can do more with less. You can operate with a lower headcount because the tools can deflect simple, repetitive customer questions. Your team can also use them to draft message responses, so you can serve more customers in the same amount of time.


This isn’t just theory. In a study of[5,179 customer support agents](https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161) , access to an AI assistant increased the number of issues agents resolved per hour by 14% on average, and by 34% for less experienced agents.


### **Reach faster resolution times**


Customers want their problems solved the first time they call. Here are two metrics to help you track this:


- **First contact resolution, or FCR.** The percentage of issues your team resolves in the first interaction, with no need for a future call back from the customer or follow-up from your reps.
- [Average handle time](https://www.quo.com/blog/average-handle-time/) **, or AHT.** How long your team spends on each conversation from start to finish. This figure includes follow-up work your reps might have to do.


AI copilots and intelligent routing improve both metrics. Routing gets customers to the right person on the first try, and copilots give reps answers without making them dig through documentation.


These things are important because[85% of CX leaders](https://www.zendesk.com/in/blog/zendesk-insights/trends/leading-in-the-ai-era-with-contextual-intelligence/) say customers will leave a brand if their issue isn’t resolved on the first contact. In addition, companies that use AI agents can expect case resolution times to drop by an[average of 20%](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/state-of-service/) .


### **Focus on high-value tasks**


When AI tackles the easy questions, your reps will get fewer support requests overall. By eliminating low-level tasks, the team can focus on higher-impact work. This might include more complex support questions, 1:1 meetings with customers, or more personalized services.


This shift is happening quickly. Salesforce recently surveyed[6,500 service professionals](https://www.salesforce.com/in/news/stories/state-of-service-report-announcement-2025/) and found that AI handles 30% of their cases today. They expect that share to reach 50% by 2027.


### **Increase customer satisfaction**


AI helps you handle customer interactions across multiple channels to meet your customers where they are. That way, your customers aren’t waiting for a reply. AI can send them the information they need. In fact, customers often know their questions don’t require human interaction, and if AI can get them answers immediately, you’ll have more[satisfied customers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-improve-customer-satisfaction/) .


According to IBM research, mature AI adopters reported[17% higher customer satisfaction](https://www.ibm.com/think/insights/customer-service-trends) . And when Salesforce asked service teams which KPI improved most after deploying AI agents, customer satisfaction[topped the list](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/ai-service-agents-improve-customer-satisfaction/) .


AI can also surface insights across your team’s interactions, allowing you to act on those insights to deliver greater business impact.


***Pro Tip:** If you’re getting a lot of support tickets, chat, or other customer requests on the same topic, you can turn the answers into a Help article. Better yet, use AI to help you draft the article. Then, add the article to your AI’s knowledge base so it can answer these questions for you in the future.*


##


**11 ways growing businesses can use customer service AI**


Let’s face it: A great customer service experience is often table stakes. Your customers want a response that’s prompt and helpful. That might mean integrating AI technology into several areas of your business, depending on the type of service you provide.


### **1. Answer every call 24/7 with an AI agent**


For small teams, missed calls are one of the most common service gaps. Calls come in during lunch, when every rep is already on the phone, or after hours. But[voicemail rarely produces customers](https://www.quo.com/blog/why-callers-dont-leave-voicemail/) .


AI agents can answer those calls for you. For example, Sona answers calls 24/7, responds to common questions using knowledge you provide, takes detailed messages, books appointments, and can even text callers during or after conversations. Every call Sona handles appears in your Quo workspace with a summary and transcript, so your team has full context if/when they decide to follow up. You can also work from Claude, ChatGPT, or Grok Bot and instruct Sona to follow up with a phone call or text on your behalf after a specific conversation.


### **2. Provide a friendly chatbot to your customers**


No one wants to get stuck in chatbot limbo. We’ve all been there: a predefined menu of issues, and none of them quite match the problem we’re having.


But AI-powered chatbots are an entirely different experience. “Chatbots are better than ever and can allow your customers to self-serve using natural language fast,” says Craig Stoss, Director of CX Transformation Delivery at PartnerHero. You can train these bots on your knowledge base, past support conversations, and brand guidelines.


US-based airline JetBlue[partnered with technology vendor ASAPP](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2023/how-generative-ai-transforms-customer-service) to provide an AI chat solution. As a result, the contact center saved more than 73,000 hours of rep time in a single quarter. On average, the customer service chatbot saves about four and a half minutes per chat. Think about what that could mean for your own business.


According to Zendesk,[71% of customers](https://www.zendesk.com/se/blog/ai/ai-impacting-cx/) agree that AI and chatbots help them get faster replies, and 77% find chatbots helpful for simple customer issues.


AI-powered chatbots can deflect easier questions so a human rep doesn’t need to be involved. These bots also offer a self-service option, so your customers don’t have to wait for a human.


### **3. Help your customer service team deliver better answers faster**


Searching for answers to customer questions slows support reps down. Whether your product is complex, you have a mountain of internal documentation, or both, your reps may get stuck.


AI-powered rep-assist tools look at historical tickets, published articles, saved templates, and other internal resources to find the right answer. These tools then draft a recommended response for the support rep, tailored to the specific case. For example, an AI-assisted app called[RightPage](https://www.zendesk.com/marketplace/apps/support/941379/rightpage/) integrates with ticketing powerhouse Zendesk to help reps resolve tickets faster and more accurately.


“These tools are especially useful for newer support team members who aren’t as familiar with your internal resources,” says Sunny Tripathi, Senior Operations Manager at Quo.


Overall, you can expect faster[first response times](https://www.quo.com/blog/first-response-time/) with rep-assist tools. And if your customer service team is subject to SLAs, they’ll help you meet the requirements with less stress.


### **4. Draft email and text messages faster to your customers**


If your customer service team drafts the same response over and over, they’re not spending their time well. Sure, you might have[customer service text templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/sample-text-messages-to-customers/) , but they still have to search for the template and add it to an email or text message.


AI can deflect email and text responses by drafting or suggesting replies and keeping the responses on-brand. When AI handles basic tickets, your team can focus on more challenging cases. Machine learning can help AI responses improve over time.


Octopus Energy, a global sustainable energy company,[added generative AI to its customer service platform](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2023/how-generative-ai-transforms-customer-service) to draft email responses. The application replies to a third of all customer inquiries. In addition to freeing up time, these emails had 18% higher customer happiness scores compared to responses generated by humans.


Support teams can leverage tools like Quo Agent, an AI assistant built into Quo. Ask our Agent questions in plain language, like which customers still need a follow-up, and it will analyze your calls, texts, and internal threads in Quo to quickly find the answer. Quo Agent can also create tasks, spot coaching opportunities, and draft replies.


### **5. Replace keypad phone menus with voice AI**


Long phone menus frustrate customers, especially when none of the options fit their problem. Voice AI lets callers explain their issue in their own words, then answers the question or sends the call to the right department or teammate. Callers get what they need on the first call, improving first-contact resolution.


At the end of the day, phone support still matters to customers. In a recent survey,[68% of participants](https://www.hospitalitynet.org/opinion/4131637/ten-ai-customer-service-statistics-for-2026-that-will-shape-your-cx-strategy) said they prefer to use the phone over digital self-service when they have a problem.


With Quo, you can pair a short phone menu with Sona. Callers who know the person or department they want to speak to can press a key. Sona can answer common questions for everyone else. By offering both options, you can cater to all kinds of callers and improve the customer experience.


### **6. Send every call to the right person with intelligent routing**


Transferring a caller two or three times is one of the fastest ways to frustrate them. Intelligent routing fixes this issue by matching each caller with the person best equipped to help.


With Quo’s AI call routing, Sona listens to the reason behind each call, then transfers the caller to the right department, teammate, or shared inbox. For example, billing questions can go straight to your office manager, while repair requests go right to your service team.


### **7. Translate support requests from international customers**


If your customer base is global — or you want it to be someday — you can use AI to offer multilingual support. Tools like Lokalise provide real-time language translation for support conversations in chat and email. AI translation tools can provide accurate responses that stay on-brand.


By providing support in your customers’ native language, you can stand out from the competition and build customer loyalty. You can also expand your reach without needing internal human resources to support additional languages.


### **8. Quickly get context on past conversations with AI summaries**


The best customer support teams do more than answer questions. You’ll stand out if your team can provide responses based on additional context about your customer and their business. This is particularly important for B2B customer service.


You can use[conversational AI for customer service](https://www.quo.com/blog/conversational-ai-customer-service/) to summarize your calls, whether they’re support calls or customer meetings. You can review the history of interactions with the customer and also get insights into their business and the challenges they face.


Customer service reps can quickly get up to speed using Quo’s AI-generated call summaries, a bullet-point list of past conversations. They can also review a full call transcription to see *exactly* what was discussed and reference the topics in future conversations with customers.


### **9. Proactively showcase your services to potential customers**


Relationships begin long before your customers sign a contract. When a customer inquires about your company, a long response listing all your products and services can feel impersonal. But customizing each reply can be time-consuming.


You can use AI to generate personalized replies based on the potential customer’s needs. For example, digital marketing agency 5K Media provides customized business strategy templates to prospective customers with an in-house AI tool. These templates are a starting point for conversations with the 5K Media team.


“The potential client might not have the resources to put the plan into action,” says Pam Abreu, Director of Client Relations at[5K Media](https://5k.co/ai/) . “We provide an opportunity to schedule a consultation with a member of our team to review what we have just put together and have the real humans do the work.”


Flow Digital, a workflow and automation consulting firm, uses AI to personalize responses to website inquiries. Instead of replying with a subject line of “Your Inquiry,” AI customizes the subject line to reflect Flow Digital Services, such as “Re: CRM Setup.” Since making the adjustment, Flow Digital has seen email open rates increase by 30% and noticed an uptick in[customer engagement](https://www.quo.com/blog/customer-engagement-framework/) and satisfaction.


### **10. Surface important CX insights and analytics**


Channel management makes overseeing customer interactions difficult. According to McKinsey, an estimated[75% of customers use multiple channels](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/the-next-frontier-of-customer-engagement-ai-enabled-customer-service) in their ongoing experience. The same customer might use email support one day, a chatbot the next, and a social media platform the day after. You must link these experiences to get an overall[customer sentiment](https://www.quo.com/blog/customer-sentiment/) analysis, whether it’s for a single user, an entire company, or your customer service interactions as a whole.


“If we don’t have an interpretive, AI-based analytics tool, we’ll be very limited with what we can analyze because there’s so much feedback to go through,” says Tripathi. “With an analytics tool, you can really look at all your feedback.” Tripathi also points out that an analytics tool can review both positive and negative feedback.


With cross-channel AI analytics, you can encompass all touchpoints, from self-service channels to rep-supported operations. “Connect all your tools to an intelligent support operations platform that can take data from across the[customer lifecycle](https://www.quo.com/blog/customer-lifecycle-management/) ,” says Stoss. “It can then give you insight into gaps in your process or areas where you can improve, \[which\] will allow you to fix problems you may not even know existed.”


### **11. Automatically categorize your calls to increase your team’s efficiency**


As your call volume grows, it’s easy to get lost in a sea of call logs. Finding the right call recording or customer snippet is a challenge for small teams.


With AI call tags, you can organize and find important calls, review key moments, and surface the ones that require attention or additional coaching, like scheduling, escalations, or problems.


Set up custom call tags in Quo to track the calls that need the most attention:


- Track customer sentiment and reach out to unhappy customers before they move to a competitor or leave a negative review.
- Track your bookings and appointments as they come in, and see which team members bring back repeat business.
- Surface your billing and invoicing requests on a weekly or monthly basis.

##


**What can go wrong and how to prevent it**


Here are common problems we see with customer service AI, and how to prevent them.


### **Inaccurate answers**


AI can sound confident, even when it’s wrong. Worse, its answers go out of date when your company’s prices, services, or policies change. For a small business, one wrong answer can cost you a customer.


To prevent this, continually train your AI. Update your knowledge base whenever something changes, review AI conversations regularly, and quickly correct everything the AI gets wrong. Only let your AI answer questions you’ve trained it for, and have it hand off to a person when it doesn’t know an answer.


In Quo, you can add knowledge to Sona by creating knowledge pages, uploading files, or importing webpages — and your edits take effect right away. You can also connect Quo to Claude, ChatGPT, or Grok Bot with the[Quo MCP](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/mcp) to review and flag specific customer conversations.


### **Losing the human touch**


As you know, customers can get frustrated when they can’t reach a person, especially for complex or urgent issues. Small businesses often win on personal service, so they can lose a lot if their AI feels cold or impersonal.


The remedy is transparency and a clear process:


- Decide which requests need a person, like complaints, billing disputes, and urgent issues.
- Make sure customers always know when they’re talking to your customer service AI agent, and that they can request a human at any time.
- Ensure your AI passes full context to your team, so they know where conversations leave off.


In Quo, you can combine a custom phone menu with conditional call routing. For example, give callers a menu option to reach your team directly, and route VIP customers to their account manager while Sona handles routine calls.


### **Data privacy and security**


AI tools can access customer details, like names, phone numbers, addresses, and service issues. Some tools store that data in ways businesses don’t expect, and some use it to train their AI models.


You can solve this problem by asking vendors how they handle customer data and whether they use it to train models. You can then decide which vendors to work with based on their answers. We also suggest only giving your AI the information it needs to do its job and limiting which team members can access customer details.


In Quo, you grant access one phone number at a time. Only the team members you add to a number can see its calls, texts, and conversation history. Quo also has Owner, Admin, and Member roles, and only Owners and Admins can change workspace roles or remove members.


### **Setup and upkeep time**


AI needs data, but small teams don’t always have time to create and maintain accurate documentation. Some AI tools also need a lot of technical setup or a long onboarding process to work the right way.


The best solution is to choose AI tools that connect to the apps you already use. That way, your team doesn’t have to learn new systems. And when it comes to your busy schedule, we suggest starting small. Document 10 to 15 common customer questions. Once you do, your AI will have the information it needs to answer the basics, and your reps can handle the rest. Also, put regular reviews on the calendar and assign one team member to oversee them.


In Quo, you add Sona to a call flow you already use. You don’t have to set up a separate tool.


### **Unpredictable costs**


Some customer service automation tools charge by the conversation, resolution, or minute, so costs are hard to predict. Using several AI tools also adds subscription costs, integration work, and admin time.


To limit billing surprises, investigate each tool’s pricing structure before you buy. Once you choose an AI tool, launch it on one use case and monitor your costs. Only add additional use cases when you’re ready. Pro tip: If possible, choose AI built into the tools you already use. Doing so will save you time and money.


In Quo, every plan includes 10 free Sona calls each month, so you can test an AI voice agent before you commit to more volume. This is a great way to minimize unpredictable costs and save money.


##


**How to implement customer service AI**


You don’t need a big budget or technical team to start with customer service AI. Follow these eight steps:


### **1. Talk to your employees**


Before you implement customer service AI, talk to your team. Explain that these tools will help them improve their work and get more done. These tools will *not* replace them.


By automating routine tasks, like answering questions about hours or pricing, AI can free your customer service reps to focus on more complex issues and customer relationships.


Also, be upfront that your reps’ roles will change. They’ll spend less time on repeat questions and more time on more meaningful work. They might take on new tasks, like reviewing AI conversations or updating your knowledge base. By addressing these concerns, you’ll make it more likely your team uses the AI tools.


### **2. Pick one problem to solve**


Don’t try to implement every change at once. Identify your biggest service gap, like missed calls, slow replies to texts, or a lack of after-hours service. Then determine if AI can help you fix it.


Whatever problem you tackle first, pick one or two metrics to track along the way. Examples include first contact resolution, resolution rate, CSAT, and response time. However, the metrics you choose will depend on the problem you want to solve. Write down where those numbers stand today so you can measure your progress.


### **3. Choose the right AI tool**


Pick a tool that solves the problem you chose in step two. For example, if you struggle with after-hours calls, an AI agent like Sona can answer them for you. When you evaluate tools, look for:


- Integrations with your current tech stack
- Affordable, predictable pricing
- Ease of use and setup
- The ability to hand conversations off to a person
- Access controls that limit who can see customer data


### **4. Build a knowledge base**


Your AI can only answer the questions you train it for. Start with 10 to 15 common customer questions. Cover the basics, like your business hours, location, service areas, and general pricing details.


Next, tell your AI which topics it should hand off to a person. That way, it doesn’t try to answer complex questions or address sensitive topics. Then assign one employee to own the AI knowledge base and update it regularly. Good knowledge management keeps your AI accurate as your business changes.


In Quo, you can add knowledge to Sona by creating pages, uploading files, or importing your website.


### **5. Set clear handoff rules**


This is important, so we’ll mention it again here: *List the requests that should always go to a person, like complaints, billing disputes, and urgent issues.* Then decide what your AI should do when it can’t help. For example, Quo’s Sona can take messages, transfer calls, and route customers to specific teammates.


Make sure your AI passes along full context so customers don’t have to repeat themselves. And set a timeframe for your team to follow up on the messages your AI takes.


### **6. Run your first test**


Test your AI before you let it interact with your customers.


Call your business number and ask common questions, plus a few tricky ones. Then launch the AI on *one* phone number and *one* use case, like after-hours calls, and adjust the tool based on performance.


In Quo, add Sona to a call flow, customize how it handles calls, and test how it performs. When you’re happy with the result, hit “Publish changes.” Sona works with business hours, so after-hours use cases are an option. Also, every Quo plan includes 10 free Sona calls, so you can easily test it before you go live.


### **7. Train your team**


Show reps how to use your AI. For example, depending on the tool you use, the AI might be able to suggest replies to support tickets or generate call summaries for future review.


Explain how to review AI conversations and flag wrong or outdated answers so the knowledge base owner can fix them. Also, set clear expectations for your team to follow up on messages the AI takes.


### **8. Review results and expand**


Finally, review AI conversations on a weekly basis. Once things are running smoothly, switch to a monthly review cadence. Compare your results to the metrics you chose in step two, and fix gaps in the knowledge base when your AI struggles. Watch customer sentiment and feedback, too, not just efficiency numbers.


Once you’re happy with the way your first use case works, add a second one. For example, expand from after-hours calls to overflow calls during busy times, or add intelligent routing.


In Quo, you can filter calls to see which ones Sona handled, and use AI call tags to track sentiment and trends.

##


**FAQs**


**What’s the difference between customer service AI and a chatbot?**


Customer service AI is the category. Chatbots are one type of customer service AI. Other types include AI agents that answer calls, voice AI that understands human language, AI copilots that help write replies, intelligent routing that sends callers to the right destination, and sentiment analysis that evaluates feelings.


**What are some examples of artificial intelligence in customer service?**


AI can help your customer service reps answer inquiries more quickly by drafting email replies or providing suggested responses. AI can also interact with customers via a chatbot, freeing up your reps for more important tasks.


**Will AI replace customer service agents?**


No. AI handles repetitive questions so your team can focus on complex, high-value conversations. Customers still want to speak with a person for urgent or sensitive issues. Agents are also needed to train the AI, review its answers, and follow up on the messages it takes.


**Is customer service AI worth it for small businesses?**


For most growing businesses, the answer is yes. AI lets small teams offer 24/7 availability and handle more requests without hiring additional employees. Results can come quickly, too. According to Salesforce,[70% of service organizations](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/ai-service-agents-improve-customer-satisfaction/) that adopt AI agents see measurable value within 60 days.


**Can AI answer phone calls for my business?**


Yes. AI agents like Quo’s Sona can answer calls 24/7, respond to common questions, take messages, book appointments, and text callers. Plus, your team gets a summary and transcript of every call Sona handles, so they can follow up with full context.


**How much does customer service AI cost?**


It depends on the tool and pricing model. Some tools charge per user, from under $10 to over $100 per month. Others charge for each conversation the AI resolves, often between $0.75 and $2. By using the AI built into the tools you already use, you can avoid stacking extra subscriptions.


**Is customer service AI safe for customer data?**


Yes, as long as you choose your vendors carefully and implement strong policies. Ask how each tool stores customer data and whether it uses that data to train AI models. Then limit which team members can access customer conversations, and only give your AI the information it needs.
